label: City of Montpelier
header:
# City of Montpelier municipal roster backfill -- Vermont
# municipal fan-out batch 15; issue #163 (VT master tracking).

sources.note: 24 App. V.S.A. ch. 005 (City of Montpelier): section 401 provides for a Mayor elected citywide to a two-year term
City of Montpelier (official website), City Council & Mayor page: lists Marc Gwinn as Mayor

24 App. V.S.A. ch. 005 (City of Montpelier): section 302 provides for two council members from each of the three voting districts, serving staggered two-year terms; section 303 provides that the Council appoints a replacement when a council vacancy has more than 90 days of unexpired term remaining
City of Montpelier (official website), City Council & Mayor page: lists the District 1 councilors as Ben Doyle (term 2025-2027) and Paul Costello (term August 12, 2026 to March 2, 2027)

City of Montpelier, City Manager's Weekly Report (July 31, 2026): announces that the District 1 seat was recently vacated by Councilmember Adrienne Gil and that the City Council would appoint a replacement on August 12, 2026 to serve until March 2, 2027; Costello holds the seat by that appointment and Gil, who departed, is not recorded
24 App. V.S.A. ch. 005 (City of Montpelier): section 302 provides for two council members from each of the three voting districts, serving staggered two-year terms
City of Montpelier (official website), City Council & Mayor page: lists the District 2 councilors as Pelin Kohn (term 2025-2027) and Sal Alfano (term 2026-2028)
24 App. V.S.A. ch. 005 (City of Montpelier): section 302 provides for two council members from each of the three voting districts, serving staggered two-year terms
City of Montpelier (official website), City Council & Mayor page: lists the District 3 councilors as Cary Brown (term 2026-2028) and Jim Sheridan (term 2025-2027)
24 App. V.S.A. ch. 005 (City of Montpelier): sections 509(a) and 905 provide for a City Clerk elected to a three-year term
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, town clerk contact spreadsheet (updated June 12, 2026): lists John Odum as Montpelier's city clerk
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, and County Officials' (January 2026): names John Odum as Montpelier's city clerk
24 App. V.S.A. ch. 005 (City of Montpelier): section 906 provides that the City Council appoints the City Treasurer; the membership is recorded as appointed
City of Montpelier (official website), staff directory: lists Crystal Lamell in the Finance Department as 'Payroll and Accounting Specialist, Treasurer'
24 App. V.S.A. ch. 005 (City of Montpelier): section 802 establishes the Parks Commission

City of Montpelier (official website), Parks Commission page: states that each Parks Commissioner is elected at Town Meeting Day to a staggered five-year term and lists the five commissioners as Emily Donaldson (term expires 2027), Andrew Brewer (2028), Kassia Randzio (Chair, 2029), Jessa Barnard (2030), and Rebecca Copans (2031)
24 App. V.S.A. ch. 005 (City of Montpelier): section 801 establishes the Green Mount Cemetery Commission

City of Montpelier (official website), Cemetery Commission page: states the Cemetery Commission consists of five members and lists Jason Kass (Chair, term expires 2027), Linda Hogan (2029), Darragh Ellerson (2026), Barbara Smith (2028), and Danielle Harris-Burnett (2030); but three cemetery seats stood at the March 3, 2026 city election (a five-year term, a one-year remainder, and a four-year remainder), which is inconsistent with the page's stagger, and the city's published 2026 cemetery results were not located -- no current holder is verified, so the post is created without memberships
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): lists fifteen Montpelier justices of the peace elected November 5, 2024

sources.note: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): lists fifteen Montpelier justices of the peace elected November 5, 2024: Conor Casey, Elaine Ball, Dona Bate, Thomas Abdelnour, Mary S. Hooper, Kimberly B. Cheney, Page Guertin, Cary Brown, John J. Mccullough III, Valerie Lewis, Sarah Carter, Judith Newman, Ron Wild, Robert Gross, and Rosie Kruger. The listing publishes no vote totals or party labels and none are recorded
